task.description: Investigate GH-352/ISS-0097 before selecting a fix direction: read tenant_context.zig and pool.zig's acquire()/applyRequestStorageRouting() mechanism; grep std.Thread.spawn across src/ (production-impact check explicitly requested by the issue) and determine for each call site whether it touches pool.acquire() on a production request-handling path; read TC-EE-10-05 in tests/integration/instance_error_test.zig to understand its thread-spawn pattern; check docs/issues/ISS-0097.json (existing) for prior context.
acceptance_criteria: Existing ISS-0097.json read and reused (not duplicated)
Every std.Thread.spawn call site in src/ individually assessed for pool.acquire()/tenant-scoped access
Any production-severity finding filed separately, not folded into this MINOR/test-only issue

result.summary: Confirmed root cause: tenant_context.zig's threadlocal storage does not propagate across std.Thread.spawn; Pool.acquire() reads it unconditionally via applyRequestStorageRouting(). Grepped std.Thread.spawn across src/ (4 call sites): webhook/dispatcher.zig CaptureServer.run and lua/timeout.zig watchdogLoop never touch pool.acquire() (test-only / atomics-only); identity/provider/bootstrap.zig KcHttpCallState.threadFn is production but pure HTTP, no DB; api/routes/onboarding.zig runSagaBackground DOES call pool.acquire() via executeSaga on a production path, but is safe by construction (public-canonical tables or explicit search_path override). Found a currently-live, separate regression of ISS-0070/GH-285 in this same call chain (persistOnboardingResult's UPDATE tenant_default.onboarding_registry, broken by GBL-134's unrelated shadow-table cleanup) — filed/updated and forwarded to the global queue per the issue-queue protocol, NOT fixed on this branch (out of scope for a MINOR/test-only issue).

issues.description: Incidental discovery: persistOnboardingResult's hardcoded UPDATE tenant_default.onboarding_registry fails post-GBL-134 (table dropped; canonical home is public). Filed as update to existing ISS-0070/GH-285 and forwarded to global queue — not fixed on this branch.
